sentences.text: Cybersecurity controls for the Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System shall be treated as operating prerequisites for safe automatic train movement after any maintenance handback.
The safety case assumes that loss of trust in communications can be as significant as loss of communications, and the operating response shall reflect that assumption.

The Cyber Security Officer shall maintain continuous monitoring of security events from the Safety Data Communication Network, the Wayside Radio Access Network, and the Metro Operations Control System.
Security monitoring shall correlate authentication failures, session resets, rejected messages, configuration changes, and abnormal timing patterns without altering any safety command path.
Alerts affecting train control availability shall be classified using operational impact, affected territory, and whether the event could change train movement authority.
The Line Traffic Controller shall be notified when a cybersecurity event requires a restriction on automatic operation or a change in communications mode.
The Cyber Security Officer uses the audit file to investigate radio session continuity and to confirm that security monitoring records are complete.
The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall be the controlled source for operational certificates used by trainborne, wayside, control center, and maintenance components.
Certificate issuance shall require approved asset identity, recorded software baseline, assigned operating domain, and confirmation that the requesting component is authorized for service.

Certificate renewal shall be planned before expiry so that the Atlas Onboard Controller, Train Radio Modem, North District Zone Controller, South District Zone Controller, and West Junction Interlocking do not enter service with degraded trust.
Falcon shall reject any control message with an invalid signature, an expired certificate, or a sequence value outside the accepted window.
Revocation shall be available for a compromised device, a retired device, or a device whose maintenance history can no longer be reconciled with approved configuration records.
The Maintenance Diagnostic Server shall not be used to bypass certificate checks or to create alternate trust paths into safety-related communications.
Administrative access to the Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall require named accounts, multifactor authentication, separation of duties, and recorded approval for privileged changes.
The Signal Maintenance Engineer may request access needed for fault isolation, but the Cyber Security Officer shall approve security-sensitive permissions before they are enabled.

The Revenue Train Operator shall not be assigned cybersecurity administration duties during passenger service, although security warnings presented in the cab shall remain part of normal operating awareness.
The Metro Operations Control System uses the Test Train Clearance Memo as a controlled prerequisite before accepting security exceptions for non-revenue movement in protected territory.

Audit evidence shall include time-synchronized event records, access approvals, certificate actions, configuration changes, alarm acknowledgements, and operator instructions related to communications security.
Audit records shall be protected from local alteration by the component that generates them and shall be retained for the period defined by Greenvale Metro governance.

The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway shall be monitored for compromise because incorrect operational context can influence control room decisions even when safety commands remain valid.
The Voice Dispatch Console shall be included in security incident procedures when a cyber event changes the normal method for issuing operational instructions.
The Platform Screen Door Controller shall accept only authenticated interfaces approved for passenger service coordination and maintenance testing.
The Dual Channel Odometer and Atlas Onboard Controller shall report security-relevant diagnostic conditions in a manner that supports investigation without exposing cryptographic material.

Security responsibilities shall be reviewed after major timetable changes, radio coverage modifications, control center upgrades, or any incident that questions the integrity of safety-related communications.
